rules: 8 of 9 archive_subtree rejections this round were a single local edit to an already-archived expression with everything else identical: swapping one price field (close for open), swapping the smoothing operator (EMA for a moving average), adding/removing an outer wrapper (rank, lag, or an extra smoothing layer), or inserting a short moving-average around one existing raw term. A single-point edit isn't enough to clear the subtree gate: change two or more structural elements at once, or change the combining operator itself.

Volume/dollar-volume expressions built only from level, threshold-count, rank-difference, or delta transforms (no price-range or return term) failed the cheap screen 4 times this round (t 0.43-0.88). The one pure-volume shape that passed was a dispersion ratio (std over mean of dollar volume): favor dispersion over level/count/rank-diff/delta when a factor has no price or return term.

Combining a raw (unranked) mean-return with a time-series-ranked liquidity measure, either by multiplying them or by using volume as an on/off filter for the return, produced very weak fitness (t=0.67 and t=0.05). Rank each side cross-sectionally before combining rather than mixing a raw term with a ranked one.

Weighting an existing up/down-day count by volume (summing volume on positive-return days) reproduced the plain unweighted count almost exactly (rho=0.881 against the archived count factor). Volume-weighting a counting factor is not a reliable way to diversify it.

Two rejections this round were exact duplicates of proposals already made earlier in the same run (a single fundamental ratio, a close-based range normalization). Check a candidate against this run's own proposal list before spending a generation call on it.

This round's accepted factors took two shapes: a pure dollar-volume dispersion ratio, and two factors pairing a range/spread term (high-low, high-open, or open-low) with dollar-volume via a cross-sectional rank product or a rank-difference, never a plain ratio of the two. Plain ratio-of-two-raw-terms variants in the spread/dollar-volume family are archive-saturated; the rank-product and rank-difference shapes are not.

A crossover call failed outright this round from exceeding the output token cap, losing that paid call for nothing. Bias crossover toward smaller/shallower parent-tree pairs so the combined output stays in budget.
